item.description: Once in a cannabis-fueled reverie I was trying to remember the name of the skanky little diner that used to be inside the Brooklyn LIRR terminal. The best I could come up with was Brelreck’s. “Breakfast at Brelreck’s” ended up as the title of a short story and a CD by The Maggies. There’s more to the story but too much to get into here. item.title: Cold Plunge
item.description: Had to wade into the frigid Mill River today to grab Trixie who was stuck in the water — no traction on all that ice! It was only about a foot deep but mighty cold, and of course I fell over a couple of times, so ended up soaked from the waist down. No permanent damage. Fortunately I had a meditative evening at Pioneer Valley Jazz Shares to process the events.

item.title: 3 Dogs (If Then Else)
item.description:
More fun with anamorphic constructions! I created the illustrations with paper, ink, and Photoshop, and laminated them to ready-made hexagonal painting panels. The custom-built beveled enclosures and the orthographic perspective in the images create the illusion of floating 3D cubes.

I also love integrating text into images. Words and letterforms are compelling to me because they’re both abstract and representational at once. My parents worked in publishing, and yes, I’m a bit of a font geek.

The bathtub image came to me first and it led to the other two. I tried to think of as many examples of “things being split 3 ways” as I could. Is it the same dog in all three pictures? Maybe, maybe not.

You can assemble these three little scenes into any number of narratives; pick one that floats your boat.

item.title: Everybody I Ever Worked With From 1980 To 1993 Or So, Drawn From Memory
item.description:
In my teenage years and 20’s, I had a ton of jobs: office-assistant-gopher at a travel bureau and an ad agency; various quick-print and xerox shops; a whole bunch of offset lithography and pre-press shops; a couple of scenic construction companies and several animation studios; plus some others I’m probably forgetting.

Whenever I left one of these jobs, I’d draw the faces of my co-workers from memory.

I can remember stories and details about some of these folks; others are completely missing from my memory.

If you recognize yourself, let me know!

Gather Up (Grant-Lee Phillips)
item.description:
Music Video for Grant-Lee Philips “Gather Up" from the album “Lightning, Show Us Your Stuff,” on Yep Roc Records.

The song’s lyrics and mood suggest the preachings of an old-time sidewalk prophet warning of imminent disaster. With this atmosphere as guide, I composited footage of Grant (it was important that he be barefoot) into a series of foreboding hand-painted environments. I’m particularly pleased with the color palette, especially the greens and yellows.

With every project I try to learn at least one new technique or process. Here I pushed myself to develop some custom particle effects (steam, fog, and windblown leaves). I also assigned randomized parameters to some elements (like the trees losing their leaves and the birds converging on the ark-spaceship) for more naturalistic choreography.

item.title: Crumbs!
item.description:
Inspired by a Franz Kafka story, this animated short answers the question of what really happens inside your toaster.
This animated short originated as a pandemic project to give me and my daughter something to do with our hands. We started with the enigmatic Franz Kafka story “The Cares of a Family Man,” which describes a mysterious object (or is it an animal?) named Odradek. As often happens, the storyboard quickly became overcomplicated and we found we were much more interested in the atmospherics than the narrative (not that the Kafka story has much of a plot). It was lockdown and we went with it, structuring it with a simple plot device about toast in a toaster. All that remains of the original concept is the one stop-motion shot of breakdancing Odradek, visible during the rave scene.

Music by Amara Jaguar.\

item.title: Take Off Your Skin
item.description: After spending a week in the hospital with a severe viral infection that caused most of my skin to fall off, I found myself humming this 1929 pop song that my mom used to sing. This film is dedicated to her memory. A light dusting of climate anxiety and body horror complement the mood. The medical image appearing on the monitor in the MRI room is the spinal column of one of my early animation studio bosses / mentors.

item.title: Dream | Fair Weather Friends Of The JFK Library
item.description: This is an oldie that I re-scanned and colored in Photoshop. One blustery day in the early 80s, Shoshana & I were walking around Columbia Point car-less and broke when we wandered into the newly opened JFK Library. The place was staffed by women who had clearly been avid JFK supporters in 1960 – they were all wearing their vintage campaign buttons and talking about JFK like they were expecting him to show up any minute – and a weird mood prevailed. We realized that it was November 22, the anniversary of JFK’s assassination.

item.title: Carolina Shout
item.description:
Another in a series of “antique music videos,” set to a 1921 composition by jazz pioneer James P. Johnson, an originator of the Harlem Stride piano style. The animation reflects the multi-leveled, over-the-top delight and frantic silliness of this amazing musical performance.

In bringing these old musical treasures to new audiences I hope to recreate in some small way the experience of hearing this music for the first time.

item.title: Dying Star (Winterpills)
item.description:
A subterranean landscape of found and archival footage forms a lush backdrop for this sad and enigmatic song by Winterpills. From the album “All My Lovely Goners” on Signature Sounds / Soft Alarm.

I started out by searching YouTube for footage of freight trains. What I found was Elizabeth Cotton singing “Freight Train” in 1957 on Pete Seeger’s TV show. (Who knew Pete Seeger had a TV show?)

Then the algorithm threw the James Baldwin footage at me, and I decided to submit to the logic of the search engine, gathering imagery using a sort of Flarf poetry approach. When I saw how Allen Ginsberg’s finger-gesture lined up with the piano riff, I had to go with it.

I threw all this footage in the blender along with some handmade artwork and a bunch of Hi-8 footage I’d shot in the NYC subway in the 1990’s. The dreamlike final shot, a view out the front window of a train barreling down tracks overgrown with weeds and trees, was (and is) incredibly mysterious and compelling to me.

item.title: Dream | Tap Dancer In Power Plant
item.description:
This enigmatic, top-hatted character appeared in a dream, performing a very solemn and dignified sort of dance. In dress and bearing he resembled some old-time hoofer like Bojangles Robinson or Sandman Sims, though it wasn’t exactly a tap dance, more a soft shoe / buck dance type of thing – anyway, it was a compelling and emotionally charged image which evoked something of my childhood immersion in old movies and my parents’ 78 records. A few years later he ended up as a character in my animated film Fishwife.

For the Fishwife dance animation, I rotoscoped video of a contemporary buck dancer whose motion had the right vibe. His name escapes me, but I do remember that tracking him down to get permission was no small feat. He was a bit confused by my asking to use his roto’d likeness in the film, and he didn’t want his name in the credits. Happily he did say yes to the whole thing.

item.title: Fish And Skulls Under Old Washington Street El, Boston, 1985
item.description:
Good old Harry The Greek’s, where I got my first pair of safety shoes.

In the background: Dudley Station on the old Orange Line elevated line. The platforms were made of wood, and a “Let’s Make Every Day Safe Driving Day” billboard, featuring a likeness of Eisenhower, remained remarkably intact 30+ years on, probably because its location directly over the tracks made it vandal-proof.

The photo was taken during a big sewer main upgrade project which turned loose an unbelievable number of rats.
